purpose: How a {{reference}} resolves, written once and asserted by BOTH
implementations: Loco.Core's WorkflowVariableResolver (which the engine runs)
and the editor's resolveReference (which 'Test Workflow' runs).
The companion of tests/shared/condition-truth-table.json, and it exists for
the same reason: the two are separate implementations in separate languages,
and they had already drifted. Probing both on identical input found the
simulator silently missing the `.data.` form the engine supports, and
resolving names in the opposite order.
It also pins a defect that was in the engine from the start and was copied
into the simulator when it was written to mirror it: a string that BOTH
begins and ends with a reference was treated as one whole reference, so
'{{user}} said {{message}}' parsed as the single path 'user}} said {{message'
and resolved to null. 'prefix {{user}} said {{message}}' worked, which is why
it survived - the failure needed a template starting AND ending with a
reference, which is exactly the shape of '{{first}} {{last}}' or '{{a}}-{{b}}'.

Lookup order is workflow variables, then node results by node id, then the
keyword 'previous' meaning the node that ran last. The engine is the
authority on this order; a variable therefore shadows a node with the same
name, including when that makes the rest of the path unresolvable.
